Responsibilities

• Evaluate business processes, data flows, and operational data to identify data integrity and quality concerns, trends, anomalies, risks, and opportunities to improve the accuracy, completeness, and effectiveness of critical business processes and outcomes.

• Leverage data analytics, reporting, automation, AI-enabled tools, and quantitative techniques to identify trends, communicate insights, and improve business outcomes.
• Develop reporting, dashboards, and visualizations that communicate performance metrics, risks, trends, and opportunities to stakeholders.
• Support governance, risk management, and continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen controls, enhance process resiliency, and increase operational effectiveness.

Required Skills

• Learning Agility: Quickly assimilates new concepts, technologies, business processes, and organizational priorities while adapting effectively to changing business needs.
• Process Excellence: Applies a process-centric mindset to understand end-to-end workflows, identify inefficiencies, evaluate controls, and support operational improvements.
• Data & Analytical Thinking: Leverages analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving techniques to evaluate complex data flows, identify risks, uncover insights, and support data-driven decision-making.
• Risk & Controls Mindset: Applies risk management principles and sound judgment to identify, assess, and mitigate operational, process, compliance, and data-related risks.
• Technology & Innovation: Utilizes data analytics, SQL, automation, AI, GenAI, process analysis, or related technologies to identify issues, improve decision-making, strengthen controls, and increase operational efficiency.
• Stakeholder Management & Communication: Strong communication, and stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to work effectively across functions, manage competing priorities, and deliver high-quality results.
• Business & Financial Acumen: Demonstrates understanding of financial services, banking, risk management, operations and governance.
• Regulated Environment Experience: Experience operating in environments where data quality, risk management, controls, compliance, and operational resiliency are critical to business performance.

Minimum Education Requirements

jobs.title: Internal Audit Executive Director – Global Audit Lead, Cybersecurity, Information Security & Cyber Resilience
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States of America, United States of America
jobs.description:
The cyber risk landscape is changing rapidly, and the Firm requires audit leadership equipped to meet the moment. We are seeking an Executive Director to lead internal audit technology coverage across the global Firm and its banking entities, including Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A. (MSBNA) and Morgan Stanley Private Bank, N.A. (MSPBNA). This role demands a forward-looking leader who can address both today's threats and the emerging risks now reshaping cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience — with deep cyber risk expertise and a strong understanding of how artificial intelligence, agentic and frontier AI models, cloud transformation, and digital assets are actively changing the risk landscape and regulatory expectations. The successful candidate will translate these developments into practical, risk-based audit strategies, deliver insightful challenge to management, and evolve the Firm's assurance approach to address current and emerging threats.

The Internal Audit Division (IAD) drives attention and resources to vulnerabilities by providing an independent and well-informed view and impactful messages about the most important risks facing our Firm. This is accomplished by performing a range of assurance activities to independently assess the quality and effectiveness of Morgan Stanley’s system of internal control, including risk management and governance systems and processes. IAD serves as an objective and independent function within the Firm’s risk management framework to foster continual improvement of risk management processes. This is an Executive Director (P6) level position within the Technical Specialist function, which is responsible for providing extensive subject matter expertise and reinforcing the ability of business and technology audit teams to appropriately assess risk and determine and execute coverage.

Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

What you’ll do in the role

• Prioritize and lead coverage of emerging risks related to artificial intelligence and frontier models — including generative and agentic AI — assessing build time, run time, and life cycle controls, data protection, identity and entitlements for autonomous agents, and the expanded attack surface these capabilities create, as well as adversaries’ growing use of AI to accelerate and scale attacks.
• Provide coverage of the idiosyncratic risks arising from cryptocurrency and digital assets, including digital asset custody, private key generation and lifecycle management, and the security of both online (network-connected) and offline (air-gapped) custody infrastructure — highlighting the associated cyber threats such as private key compromise, transaction and address manipulation, smart contract exploitation, and the irreversible loss of assets.
• Assess quantum computing and post-quantum cryptography readiness, and other frontier technology risks, ensuring these are reflected in the audit plan and in the Firm’s forward-looking resilience posture.
• Monitor the intensifying threat landscape — including advanced attack techniques and regulatory change — and continuously factor emerging threats into audit scoping and assurance coverage.
• Provide independent assurance over the design and operating effectiveness of the controls that protect the Firm’s and Banks’ technology environment, customer data, and critical business services
• Set and lead the multi-year, risk-based audit strategy for cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience across the Firm and its Banks, spanning the full technology stack (infrastructure, network, platform, application, and data layers) and each business unit to form an integrated, Firm-wide view of control effectiveness, and how cyber threats, information loss, and a cyber attach could affect business lines, critical services, and legal entities across the Firm.
• Direct execution of the audit plan across the core cyber and information security domains — identity and access management, endpoint security, network security, data protection, threat detection and response, and vulnerability management.
• Lead assurance activities assessing cyber resilience capabilities, including incident response, disaster recovery, business continuity, and third-party/vendor security.
• Evaluate compliance with regulatory expectations (e.g., FFIEC, OCC, FDIC, NYDFS, GLBA, RGF, DORA) and industry frameworks (CRI Profile, NIST CSF, ISO 27001).
• Oversee root cause analysis on control failures and audit findings, and track remediation to closure.
• Comprehensively articulate actionable insights regarding the criticality and impact of cyber risk, and how well it is managed, to senior management and regulators. Prepare materials for the Chief Audit Executive’s updates to the Audit Committee and the Board,
• Coordinate with second-line risk and compliance functions and with external auditors and regulators, and collaborate with global peers to identify risk themes and implications across business segments and legal entities.
• Mentor and develop audit staff and manage a global team; help inform and address talent needs and identify stretch and development opportunities for team members.

What you’ll bring to the role

• Advanced understanding of cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience risks and the relevant regulations, including banking regulatory requirements.
• Experience assessing emerging technology risks and their control implications — including AI and agentic AI, frontier models, cryptocurrency and digital asset custody, and quantum/post-quantum cryptography — and the ability to translate a rapidly changing threat landscape into practical audit coverage.
• Strong knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CRI Profile) and experience auditing identity and access management, cloud security, and network architecture.
• Expertise in audit principles, methodology, tools, and processes (e.g., risk assessments, planning, testing, reporting, and continuous monitoring).
• Ability to analyze data and prioritize coverage and assurance activities based on the criticality of risk.
• Ability to articulate risk and impact clearly and succinctly to different audiences, including senior stakeholders, the Board, and regulators.
• Ability to inspire and support others to do their best work through active coaching, feedback, and development opportunities, and by ensuring trust and inclusion among team members.
• Experience in overseeing resource utilization and monitoring progress against deliverables.
• A bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Computer Science, or a related field.
• At least 12-15 years’ relevant experience in IT/cyber audit, information security, or risk management — ideally in banking or financial services — would generally be expected to fulfill the skills required for this role.
• Relevant certifications (e.g., CISA, CISSP, CISM, or equivalent) preferred.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience with incident response or red team/penetration testing programs.
• Familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
• Prior experience at a large financial institution or a Big 4 consulting firm.

Our values — putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back — aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what’s best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. Global Realty Services (GRS) is seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented Governance, Risk, and Technology Analyst to support technology governance, lease administration, recovery and resolution planning (RRP), workplace technology platforms, portfolio administration, and strategic technology initiatives across the organization.

This role combines responsibilities associated with lease administration, workplace technology management, data governance, operational resilience, and technology innovation. The ideal candidate possesses strong analytical skills, enjoys solving complex business problems, is comfortable working with large data sets and technology platforms, and has an interest in evaluating emerging technologies that enhance workplace experiences, portfolio management, operational resilience, and business performance.

Recovery & Resolution Planning (RRP) Support

Business Resilience Manager (Solventum)

The Impact You’ll Make in this Role

The Business Resilience Manager will lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of Solventum’s enterprise Business Resilience program. The role will establish the governance, methodologies, standards, tools, and assurance activities necessary to strengthen organizational preparedness, response, recovery, and resilience across Solventum’s global operations.

Working within Global Security and in close partnership with business units and functions, the Manager will coordinate Business Resilience with Crisis Management, Technology Resilience, Cybersecurity Incident Response, Manufacturing and Operational Technology resilience, Supply Chain, Enterprise Risk Management, and other related disciplines. The role will help ensure that business-defined recovery requirements, technology recovery capabilities, operational dependencies, and crisis decision-making processes are aligned.

The Manager will lead enterprise Business Impact Analysis and continuity-planning cycles, establish minimum program and plan requirements, maintain an integrated view of critical business services and dependencies, oversee exercising and corrective-action management. The role will also support the delivery of Internal Audit and management remediation commitments related to business resilience.

This is a hands-on program management role requiring the ability to translate strategy and audit requirements into practical methodologies, accountable workstreams, measurable outcomes, and sustainable business practices.

Program Governance

Lead the operationalization of Solventum’s Business Resilience governance framework.

Develop and maintain the BCM operating model, program charter, policies, procedures, methodologies, standards, and annual program plan.

Identify and implement opportunities to leverage artificial intelligence and automation to strengthen business resilience capabilities, including risk identification, scenario analysis, business impact analysis, crisis preparedness and response.

Serve as principal program lead for the BCM system and associated program data.

Coordinate alignment across Business Continuity, Crisis Management, Technology Resilience, Cybersecurity Incident Response, Manufacturing and Operational Technology resilience, Supply Chain resilience, Enterprise Risk Management, and other related programs.

Monitor remediation progress, challenge delays or gaps, escalate material risks, and prepare regular status updates for program and executive governance bodies.

Design and facilitate discussion-based and operational exercises that test governance, plans, recovery strategies, communication methods, dependencies, and decision-making.

Establish an exception-management process for business areas unable to meet BCM standards or documented recovery requirements.

Maintain defensible evidence supporting program implementation, control operation, management oversight, and remediation closure.

Establish a consistent after-action process, including observations, root causes, accountable corrective actions, target dates, validation evidence, and closure approval.

Champion responsible adoption of AI-enabled tools and emerging technologies to improve resilience insights, accelerate decision-making, and enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the business resilience program.

Business Impact Analysis and Continuity Risk

At Gilead, we’re creating a healthier world for all people. For more than 35 years, we’ve tackled diseases such as HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19 and cancer – working relentlessly to develop therapies that help improve lives and to ensure access to these therapies across the globe. We continue to fight against the world’s biggest health challenges, and our mission requires collaboration, determination and a relentless drive to make a difference.

Every member of Gilead’s team plays a critical role in the discovery and development of life-changing scientific innovations. Our employees are our greatest asset as we work to achieve our bold ambitions, and we’re looking for the next wave of passionate and ambitious people ready to make a direct impact.

We believe every employee deserves a great leader. People Leaders are the cornerstone to the employee experience at Gilead and Kite. As a people leader now or in the future, you are the key driver in evolving our culture and creating an environment where every employee feels included, developed and empowered to fulfil their aspirations. Join Gilead and help create possible, together.

Job Description

Reporting administratively to Andy Dickinson, Chief Financial Officer, and with direct access to the Audit Committee of the Board of Directors, the Vice President, Head of Audit & Risk Management will lead Gilead’s global Internal Audit, enterprise risk management and business continuity functions. This executive will provide independent and objective assurance regarding the effectiveness of the company’s governance, risk management, internal controls and business processes, while also leading the company’s enterprise-wide risk management and business continuity frameworks. The role will serve as a trusted advisor to the Audit Committee, Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and senior leadership team, providing clear perspectives on Gilead’s most significant and emerging risks and helping ensure that risk considerations are appropriately incorporated into enterprise decision-making.

Leading an established global organization, the Vice President, Head of Audit & Risk Management will have the opportunity to shape the next evolution of the function. Gilead has built a strong foundation and has begun investing in new technologies and approaches to enhance audit effectiveness. The next leader will build on this progress, bringing a forward-looking perspective on how technology, data, automation and artificial intelligence can enable more continuous and predictive approaches to audit and risk management.

This executive will lead a risk-based audit strategy spanning Gilead’s global operations and evolving risk landscape, including financial, operational, commercial, compliance, technology, cybersecurity, supply chain and manufacturing-related risks. In parallel, the role will lead Gilead’s broader enterprise risk management and governance framework, providing senior leadership and the Audit Committee with an integrated and forward-looking perspective on the company’s most significant and emerging risks. As Gilead continues to transform, including through the increasing adoption of AI and other emerging technologies, this leader will ensure that the company’s audit coverage, risk governance and control environment evolve alongside the business.

The Vice President, Head of Audit & Risk Management will operate with the independence required of the Internal Audit function while developing strong and constructive relationships throughout Gilead. This individual will communicate regularly with the Audit Committee and will have the credibility and executive presence to engage directly with Gilead’s CEO and senior leadership team, ensuring that significant risks and issues are surfaced early and communicated at the appropriate level of depth.

This role will be based at Gilead’s headquarters in Foster City, California, and will include travel to Gilead’s affiliates and operations globally.

Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Internal Audit & Assurance

• Develop and execute a comprehensive, risk-based Internal Audit strategy aligned with Gilead’s strategic priorities, operating environment and evolving enterprise risk profile.
• Lead the annual audit planning and risk assessment process, maintaining the flexibility to adjust audit priorities as business conditions and emerging risks evolve.
• Provide independent assurance across financial, operational, commercial, compliance and technology-related risks and controls, including areas such as cybersecurity, data, supply chain and manufacturing.
• Evaluate the effectiveness of governance, risk management, internal controls and key business processes and provide practical, actionable recommendations that strengthen the organization while enabling the business.
• Oversee the execution and quality of audits across Gilead’s global operations and affiliates and ensure significant findings and remediation plans are appropriately tracked and communicated.
• Maintain appropriate coordination with external auditors and other assurance and compliance functions to ensure effective coverage of enterprise risks and minimize unnecessary duplication.

Enterprise Risk Management & Risk Governance

• Lead Gilead’s enterprise risk management framework and associated governance processes, ensuring a comprehensive and forward-looking view of the company’s principal and emerging risks, including cybersecurity, AI and other rapidly evolving areas of enterprise risk.
• Facilitate enterprise risk identification and assessment across the organization, partnering with senior leaders and risk owners to evaluate risk exposure, mitigation strategies and changes in the business and external environment.
• Provide an integrated view of enterprise risk to senior management and the Audit Committee, identifying themes, interdependencies and emerging issues that warrant leadership attention.
• Continue evolving the company’s risk management approach toward more dynamic and continuous risk monitoring, leveraging data and technology to identify changes in risk indicators earlier.

Audit & Risk Transformation

• Set the vision and roadmap for the continued modernization of Internal Audit and risk management, building on the organization’s existing foundation while identifying opportunities to adopt leading practices.
• Accelerate the use of technology, data analytics, automation and AI across the audit lifecycle, including risk assessment, planning, testing, monitoring and reporting.
• Partner with technology, cybersecurity and business leaders as Gilead expands its use of AI and other emerging technologies, ensuring that related risks, governance and controls are appropriately incorporated into the company’s audit and enterprise risk frameworks.

Business Continuity Management (BCM)

Business Continuity Management (BCM) lead the development, implementation, and maintenance of the overarching Business Continuity Management framework, policies, and resilience strategies.

Responsibilities include:

• Business Impact Analysis (BIA): Lead organization-wide BIAs to identify critical business processes, operational dependencies, and recovery time/point objectives.
• Plan Development: Oversee the creation and regular updating of Business Continuity Plans (BCP) and technical Disaster Recovery (DR) strategies in partnership with IT and department heads.
• Testing & Simulation: Design and facilitate tabletop exercises, functional drills, and full-scale disaster simulations to validate readiness and uncover gaps.

Executive & Audit Committee Partnership

• Serve as a principal advisor to the Audit Committee on Internal Audit and enterprise risk management matters, providing clear, independent perspectives on significant risks, audit findings, control matters and remediation progress.
• Maintain direct and effective communication with the Audit Committee and ensure the function has the independence, access and authority necessary to fulfill its responsibilities.
• Develop trusted relationships with the CEO, CFO and senior leadership team, communicating significant and emerging issues early and translating complex risk matters into clear, decision-relevant insights.
• Provide regular updates to Gilead’s senior leadership on the enterprise risk landscape and help facilitate thoughtful discussion of emerging risks and mitigation priorities.
• Balance independence and professional skepticism with a collaborative, pragmatic approach that enables Internal Audit and risk management to serve as valued partners to the business.

Team Leadership & Organizational Development

• Lead, develop and mentor Gilead’s global Audit & Risk Management organization, fostering a culture of integrity, intellectual curiosity, accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
• Cultivate a high-performing audit and risk function, leveraging audit, risk, technology, analytics, and business expertise to support Gilead’s evolving needs.
• Develop emerging leaders and strengthen succession planning while creating opportunities for team members to broaden their experience and impact across the organization.
• Build a technology-forward mindset across the team and ensure professionals are developing the skills required for an increasingly data-driven, AI-enabled audit and risk environment.
• Establish clear priorities and performance expectations while maintaining the agility to deploy resources toward Gilead’s most significant and rapidly evolving risks.

Candidate Profile

The successful candidate will be a seasoned Internal Audit and risk management executive with significant experience operating within a complex, global public company. They will bring broad expertise across internal audit, enterprise risk management, governance, internal controls and compliance, coupled with strong business acumen and a demonstrated ability to translate enterprise risks into practical, actionable insights. The ideal candidate will have a track record of leading a sophisticated audit and risk organization while advancing the function through technology, data analytics, automation and AI-enabled capabilities.

Gilead is seeking a forward-thinking leader who is intellectually curious and energized by the opportunity to continue evolving how Internal Audit and risk management support the enterprise. This individual will bring a progressive perspective on the future of the function, including the use of technology, data analytics, automation and AI to enhance audit effectiveness, enable more continuous risk monitoring and identify emerging issues earlier. They will be comfortable challenging established ways of working while thoughtfully building on the strengths of an experienced organization.

The Vice President, Head of Audit & Risk Management will be a highly credible and collaborative enterprise leader who combines independence and professional judgment with a pragmatic, business-oriented approach. They will have the executive presence and communication skills to establish trusted relationships with the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, senior leadership team and Audit Committee, translating complex audit and risk matters into clear perspectives at the appropriate level of detail. The individual will be equally effective engaging deeply with business and functional leaders across the organization while maintaining the independence and objectivity required of the Internal Audit function.

The successful candidate will also be an engaging people leader with a demonstrated commitment to developing high-performing teams and creating opportunities for talent to grow. They will lead a team of 25 professionals, fostering a collaborative and inclusive environment while continuing to build capabilities across technology, data analytics, AI and emerging areas of risk. This leader will bring the team along in the continued evolution of the function, encouraging new ways of working while building on the expertise and strong foundation already in place.

The ideal candidate will have experience within the following areas:

• 15+ years of progressive experience across Internal Audit, enterprise risk management, public accounting, finance, controls and/or related disciplines within complex, global organizations.
• Significant experience leading a global internal audit function for a publicly traded multinational company.
• Broad expertise across risk-based internal audit, enterprise risk management, governance, internal controls, SOX, compliance, operational risk and technology risk.
• Demonstrated experience owning or meaningfully leading enterprise risk management and risk governance, including identifying and assessing emerging risks and effectively communicating the enterprise risk profile to senior leadership and the Board.
• Demonstrated success modernizing Internal Audit and risk management through technology, advanced analytics, automation, continuous auditing and AI-enabled capabilities.
• Experience navigating complex, highly regulated operating environments; pharmaceutical or life sciences experience is valued but not required.
• Experience assessing risks across a broad operating environment, including commercial activities, technology and cybersecurity, supply chain, manufacturing and other enterprise processes.
• Strong understanding of professional Internal Audit standards and public-company governance and control requirements.
• Proven ability to lead, develop and mentor high-performing teams while building organizational capability and developing future leaders.
• Significant experience interacting with Audit Committees and Boards of Directors, with the executive presence, judgment and communication skills to engage credibly with the CEO and other senior executives.
• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related discipline; CPA, CIA, CISA and/or an advanced degree is preferred.

People Leader Accountabilities:

• Create Inclusion : Model inclusive leadership and embed diversity, equity, and inclusion into how the team operates, makes decisions, and develops talent.
